'''''007 First Light''''' is a 2026 [[action-adventure video game]] developed and published by [[IO Interactive]]. Based on the ''[[James Bond]]'' franchise, it tells an original narrative inspired by [[List of James Bond novels and short stories|the novels and short stories]] by [[Ian Fleming]], and the [[Portrayal of James Bond in film|film series]] starring the character. The game depicts [[James Bond (literary character)|James Bond]]'s origin story, as he embarks on the mission he must complete to earn his licence to kill.

Following the release of ''[[007 Legends]]'' (2012), publisher [[Activision]] had its non-exclusive licence to produce [[James Bond in video games|''James Bond'' video games]] revoked, resulting in an extended hiatus of video games adaptations. IO Interactive announced the development of a ''James Bond'' game in November 2020. The game entered full production at IO Interactive following the completion of ''[[Hitman 3]]'' (2021), and was fully revealed in June 2025.

''007 First Light'' was released for [[PlayStation 5]], [[Windows]], and [[Xbox Series X/S]] on 27 May 2026, with a [[Nintendo Switch 2]] version scheduled for later in the year. The game received generally positive reviews from critics, with praise given to the gameplay, combat, writing, and [[Patrick Gibson (actor)|Patrick Gibson]]'s performance as Bond. It had sold 4 million units by August 2026.

== Gameplay ==
{{More citations needed|section|date=June 2026}}
[[File:007FL game screenshot.jpg|thumb|300px|Bond can use the laser from his Q-Watch to stun enemies.]]
Players control James Bond as he goes through training and executes missions to become a fully-fledged MI6 agent. The game is played from a third-person perspective, with occasional quick-time events and cutscenes. 

As Bond, players participate in operations to advance the story, culminating in him "[[00 Agent|earning the number]]". Players may choose to complete missions aggressively, fighting enemies and taking them down, or by using bluffs and environmental items to slip past enemies and talk their way out of trouble. 

Bond is able to parry opponents' attacks and perform takedowns to neutralize them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Obenza |first=Myles |date=30 April 2026 |title=007 First Light Hands-On: A Fun James Bond That Plays It Safe |url=https://kotaku.com/over-3-hours-with-007-first-light-a-bond-game-thats-a-ton-of-fun-despite-playing-it-safe-2000692050 |access-date=2 June 2026 |website=Kotaku |language=en-US}}</ref> While Bond is usually restricted to non-lethal means of combat when engaging enemies, he may be granted a "licence to kill" when enemies show the intent to kill him, permitting Bond to use lethal force, including the use of firearms.<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 April 2026 |title=Playing 007: First Light makes me wonder if it's actually possible to nail James Bond - but developer IOI has made a cracking attempt |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/007-first-light-game-preview-james-bond-hands-on-interview |access-date=2 June 2026 |work=Eurogamer.net |language=en |quote=That's defined here by the 'license to kill' mechanic, whereby you're only able to use lethal force when an enemy shows lethal intent first.}}</ref>

''007 First Light'' features an [[Omega SA|Omega]] [[Omega Seamaster|Seamaster]] chronograph watch specially designed for the game,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Austin |first1=Tom |date=25 December 2025 |title=The most interesting Omega watch of 2025, that hasn't actually released... yet |url=https://timeandtidewatches.com/the-most-interesting-omega-watch-of-2025-that-hasnt-actually-released-yet/ |website=Time+Tide |language=en-US |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hart |first=Spencer |date=6 October 2025 |title=Omega drops a trailer for the next James Bond, and it's all about the watch |url=https://www.stuff.tv/news/omega-drops-a-trailer-for-the-next-james-bond-and-its-all-about-the-watch/ |website=Stuff |language=en-US |access-date=10 December 2025}}</ref> alongside the [[Aston Martin Valhalla]] sports car.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cripe |first=Michael |date=20 November 2025 |title=James Bond Hops into a Souped-Up Aston Martin in Vehicle-Themed 007 First Light Trailer |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/james-bond-hops-into-a-souped-up-aston-martin-in-vehicle-themed-007-first-light-trailer |website=IGN |language=en-US |access-date=10 December 2025}}</ref> Q's lab is responsible for supplying Bond's mission attire, weapons, equipment and vehicles. Bond's main tool on his missions is the Q Watch, a modified Omega Seamaster Diver 300M which can hack electronics, and he can bring other gadgets to use on his missions.{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}}

=== Plot ===
<!-- Per [[MOS:VGPLOT]], word count is recommended to not exceed 700 words. Current word count: 686 -->
A [[Special Air Service]] team is ambushed during a retrieval operation in Iceland, leaving [[Fleet Air Arm|Navy aircrewman]] James Bond the sole survivor. Guided by an MI6 handler, he reaches the target{{em dash}}a research camp studying a crashed satellite{{em dash}}finding it occupied by a mercenary group. Defying orders, Bond rescues the captive scientists and destroys the camp, preventing the asset from falling into enemy hands.

Bond is recruited by M, the head of MI6, to join the revitalised 00 program. Despite starting months behind the six other candidates, he passes the training under the strict regimen of his reluctant instructor, John Greenway. He grows close to his team, especially recruits Monroe and Cressida. A few months later, the team is tasked with apprehending Rhys Beckett, a rogue agent and former 009, at a hotel in Slovakia. Bond follows a suspicious staff member revealed to be one of twin assassins, the Murtos, who fatally stab Monroe and set off a bomb that kills two other recruits and cripples Cressida. Before Beckett escapes, Bond attaches a wristwatch to his plane, allowing MI6 to track him to [[Mauritania]].

Bond and Greenway set off to capture Beckett but discover that he has been killed. They deduce that Beckett was the target of the bombing rather than the mastermind, but the proof is destroyed in a mercenary ambush. Despite Bond and Greenway suspecting a larger plot, M declares Beckett responsible for the bombing and closes the case. One of the Murto twins attacks Bond at home; Bond chases him to a gala hosted by [[AI]] pioneer Sir Nicholas Webb and kills him. He finds evidence incriminating Webb for the bombing in Slovakia and learns Greenway is also a target.

Bond is captured by Webb's son Damien and is rescued by Isola Vale, a professional thief he met while she was masquerading as a French agent in Slovakia. He reunites with Greenway, who has killed the assassins sent after him. The pair infiltrate Webb Industries' headquarters and, with Isola's help, learn that Webb's actions are cover-ups for mistakes committed by his quantum [[supercomputer]], THEIA, which is being employed by MI6 to predict terrorist threats. THEIA's first mistake was [[Hallucination (artificial intelligence)|falsely identifying]] Beckett and two other agents as [[Mole (espionage)|moles]], whom Greenway was sent to eliminate, with Webb having murdered Beckett to prevent him from exposing THEIA's flaws. Shocked by the revelation, Greenway goes off-grid.

Despite orders to bring both agents in on terrorism charges, M sends Bond to a luxury resort in Vietnam to gather evidence on Webb's duplicity and intercept Damien, who plans to conduct another cover-up by murdering geneticist Theresa Lorca. Bond saves Lorca and kills the other Murto twin but is captured by Damien in the process. After being freed by Greenway, Bond seemingly kills Damien by crushing him under pipes. Greenway, fatally wounded in the encounter, admits in his final moments that Bond is what MI6 needs and his heroic nature is what defines him.

Webb coerces M into granting him immunity by leaking vital MI6 information. Unwilling to accept such an outcome, Bond goes rogue and teams up with Isola to infiltrate Webb's facility in [[Antarctica]], where he discovers Webb's scheme to supplant the British government with THEIA's sibling AI, HYPERION. Bond fights his way to HYPERION's core, but Isola fatally shoots Webb and steals the core for herself. Bond manages to stop Isola and destroy the core, and both are taken into MI6 custody. They are freed when mercenaries attack MI6 headquarters. While Isola flees, Bond heads to THEIA's chamber, finding Damien stealing THEIA's core. After dispatching the mercenaries with a customized [[Aston Martin Valhalla]], Bond chases Damien into the sewers, disables his exo-suit, and throws himself and Damien into the reservoir below. Damien drowns while Bond is saved by Isola, who kisses him before making off with THEIA's core.

At Greenway's grave, M informs Bond that he has been cleared of all charges and formally inducts him into the "00" program. Designating himself 007 in honour of being the seventh recruit, Bond vows to track Isola down to recover the THEIA core and find out for whom she works.

==Development==
''007 First Light'' is the first major [[James Bond in video games|game featuring James Bond]] following a hiatus resulting from the critical and commercial failure of ''[[007 Legends]]'' (2012), which saw publisher [[Activision]] having its non-exclusive licence to produce video games using the ''James Bond'' [[intellectual property]] (IP) [[revoked]] by [[Eon Productions]] and [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer]] in January 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Activision loses James Bond licence? |url=https://metro.co.uk/2013/01/04/activision-loses-james-bond-licence-3338164/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250607195237/https://metro.co.uk/2013/01/04/activision-loses-james-bond-licence-3338164/ |archive-date=7 June 2025 |website=[[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]] |date=1 April 2013 |access-date=5 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sinclair |first=Brendan |date=1 April 2013 |title=Activision ''007'' games pulled from digital stores |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/activision-007-games-pulled-from-digital-stores |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250607195237/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/activision-007-games-pulled-from-digital-stores/ |archive-date=7 June 2025 |website=GamesIndustry.biz |access-date=5 June 2025}}</ref> The IP licensing agreement for IO Interactive's game was later brokered by Delphi Interactive with [[Danjaq]], the holding company that owns Eon Productions, and Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eriksen |first=Kaare |date=31 October 2024 |title=Delphi Interactive’s Leadership on Challenging Gaming’s ‘Publisher Industrial Complex,’ Hiring Ex-Nordisk Games Chief Mikkel Weider (EXCLUSIVE) |url=https://variety.com/2024/gaming/news/delphi-interactive-nordisk-games-mikkel-weider-strictly-business-1236192058/ |access-date=30 June 2026 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

''[[Hitman (franchise)|Hitman]]'' series developer [[IO Interactive]] met with Eon Productions to pitch their own vision for a ''James Bond'' video game as they were developing ''[[Hitman 3]]'' (2021). According to company president Hakan Abrak, the studio was under the impression that "[Eon] were not looking for a game", having grown dissatisfied with the action-oriented style and gameplay of the latest console ''Bond'' games under Activision.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fillari |first=Alessandro |date=7 November 2023 |title=Before Project 007 was greenlit, the ''Hitman'' studio had to convince the ''James Bond'' rights-holders to give video game adaptations another shot: "They were not looking for a game" |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/before-project-007-was-greenlit-the-hitman-studio-had-to-convince-the-james-bond-rights-holders-to-give-video-game-adaptations-another-shot-they-were-not-looking-for-a-game/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250607195237/https://www.gamesradar.com/before-project-007-was-greenlit-the-hitman-studio-had-to-convince-the-james-bond-rights-holders-to-give-video-game-adaptations-another-shot-they-were-not-looking-for-a-game/ |archive-date=7 June 2025 |website=[[GamesRadar+]] |language=en-GB |access-date=21 April 2025}}</ref> Chief creative officer Christian Elverdam stated that a move away from relying on weapons to complete missions was an integral part of the studio's pitch to Eon, citing their work on ''Hitman'' as a game where violent solutions were actively discouraged, as an example of how Eon were convinced by IO Interactive that there was a "sophistication" in how the developers approached espionage gameplay.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spencer |first=Alex |date=4 January 2024 |title=From ''Hitman'' to ''007'' and everything between – Edge magazine goes behind the scenes with IO Interactive |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/from-hitman-to-007-and-everything-between-edge-magazine-goes-behind-the-scenes-with-io-interactive/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250627092009/https://www.gamesradar.com/from-hitman-to-007-and-everything-between-edge-magazine-goes-behind-the-scenes-with-io-interactive/ |archive-date=27 June 2025 |website=[[GamesRadar+]] |language=en-GB |access-date=21 April 2025}}</ref> IO Interactive emphasised its interest in pursuing an original interpretation of [[James Bond (literary character)|James Bond]], divorced from any of the prior literary and [[James Bond (film character)|cinematic incarnations]] of the character, as they wished to apply a similar effort to creating their own narrative for an existing IP as they did for any of their original projects and characters.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barnett |first=Brian |date=5 April 2021 |title=Hitman Dev's ''James Bond'' Game Is an Original Story Drawing From the Franchise's Entire History |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/hitman-devs-james-bond-game-is-an-original-story-drawing-from-the-franchises-entire-history-ign-unfiltered/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250805191955/https://www.ign.com/articles/hitman-devs-james-bond-game-is-an-original-story-drawing-from-the-franchises-entire-history-ign-unfiltered/ |archive-date=5 August 2025 |website=IGN |language=en-US |access-date=21 April 2025}}</ref> This includes the likeness of James Bond himself, which is not derived from any of the actors to [[portrayal of James Bond in film|portray him on film]], a first for the character in a [[player character|playable]] capacity since ''[[James Bond 007: Agent Under Fire]]'' (2001).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oloman |first=Jordan |date=26 January 2021 |title=''Hitman'' Developer's ''James Bond'' Won't Be Based on Any Previous Actor |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/hitman-developers-james-bond-wont-be-based-on-any-previous-actor/ |url-status=live |language=en-US |access-date=1 May 2025}}</ref>

Elverdam was excited at the prospect of having a version of James Bond produced from the ground up for gaming, remarking on how it removed expectations that their version of the character would have to adhere to characteristics of pre-existing iterations while also being a take on the property "gamers can call their own". He additionally recalled a trip that the development team had made to [[Pinewood Studios]] during production of the film ''[[No Time to Die]]'' (2021), which instilled the "gravity" of taking on the ''Bond'' licence.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Purchese |first=Robert |date=16 March 2023 |title=''Hitman'' studio IO opens up a little about its ''James Bond 007'' game |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/hitman-studio-io-opens-up-a-little-about-its-james-bond-007-game/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250826012311/https://www.eurogamer.net/hitman-studio-io-opens-up-a-little-about-its-james-bond-007-game/ |archive-date=26 August 2025 |website=[[Eurogamer]] |access-date=21 April 2025}}</ref> According to Abrak, the idea of depicting James Bond's origin and efforts to claim his licence to kill, an event only definitively and briefly portrayed in the opening of the [[Daniel Craig]] film ''[[Casino Royale (2006 film)|Casino Royale]]'' (2006), was enthusiastically received between IO Interactive and Eon, who were both receptive to the idea of a narrative that is "completely beginning and becoming a story" as opposed to directly adapting the plot of an existing ''Bond'' film.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Kat |date=16 October 2024 |title=Project 007 Is a 'Young Bond for Gamers' and Hopefully the Start of a New Trilogy, IO Interactive Boss Says |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/project-007-io-interactive-young-bond-for-gamers-trilogy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250901175607/https://www.ign.com/articles/project-007-io-interactive-young-bond-for-gamers-trilogy |archive-date=1 September 2025 |website=IGN |language=en-US |access-date=21 April 2025}}</ref> The game's art director, Rasmus Poulsen, stated that the team sought to avoid portraying [[criticism of James Bond|certain aspects of the character]] that were [[exploitation of women in mass media|deemed outdated]], and in particular, [[societal attitudes towards women|attitudes towards women]] seen expressed by Bond in previous series entries that the developers believed would be perceived as [[sexist]] by modern audiences.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Addison |first=Luke |date=10 September 2025 |title=007 First Light Franchise Art Director Admits Steps Were Taken to Avoid Certain 'Traits' of Bond |url=https://thethumbwars.com/007-first-light-art-director-interview-james-bond/ |website=Thumb Wars |language=en-US |access-date=12 September 2025}}</ref>

Production on ''007 First Light'' began with a small team initially while most of IO Interactive were finishing work on ''Hitman 3'' (2021) before scaling up. Development took place across IO Interactive's five studios in [[Copenhagen]], [[Malmo]], [[Istanbul]], [[Barcelona]] and [[Brighton]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cieslak |first1=Marc |date=24 May 2026 |title=New James Bond game shows more vulnerable side to iconic British spy |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvgzdr177mvo |website=BBC News |language=en-GB |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref> ''007 First Light'' was IO Interactive's most expensive title to develop with its budget before marketing at over $100 million.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gach |first1=Ethan |date=5 May 2026 |title=Despite James Bond Being Its Most Expensive Game Ever, Hitman Maker Says Blockbusters 'Can Be Done For Half Of What You Hear About' |url=https://kotaku.com/despite-james-bond-being-its-most-expensive-game-ever-hitman-maker-says-blockbusters-can-be-done-for-half-of-what-you-hear-about-2000693247 |website=Kotaku |language=en-US |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref> IO Interactive did not use [[generative AI]] in the development of ''007 First Light''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Makuch |first1=Eddie |date=1 May 2026 |title=Two More High-Profile Games Say No To GenAI |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/two-more-high-profile-games-say-no-to-genai/1100-6539745/ |website=GameSpot |language=en-US |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref> Art director Rasmus Poulsen said that a theme of Bond is often "beware of utopia" as the game's narrative deals with the intersection between artificial intelligence and its fallible role in decision-making for defence companies.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tansell |first1=Chris |date=30 April 2026 |title="The thematics of Bond are often: beware of utopia" - 007: First Light art director says developer IO Interactive hasn't used any generative AI to make it |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/007-first-light-dev-not-using-gen-ai-beware-utopia-bond-theme |website=Eurogamer |language=en-GB |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref> IO Interactive sought to "reinforce the immersion" of Bond as a British spy by excising any [[Glossary of American terms not widely used in the United Kingdom|Americanisms]]. In the game's State of Play demo from September 2025 showcasing the Slovakia section, Bond used the [[American English]] phrase "parking lot" which was changed to the [[British English|British]] "car park" in the final game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Phillips Kennedy |first1=Victoria |date=28 May 2026 |title=IOI is 'keeping the British end up' in 007 First Light by switching out Americanisms to "reinforce the immersion" |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/007-first-light-americanism-parking-lot |website=Eurogamer |language=en-GB |access-date=31 May 2026}}</ref> On 13 May 2026, it was announced that ''007 First Light'' had "gone gold" with principal development complete and the game sent to physical disc manufacturing.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Croft |first1=Liam |date=13 May 2026 |title=007 First Light Now Ready for Action, James Bond PS5 Game Goes Gold |url=https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2026/05/007-first-light-now-ready-for-action-james-bond-ps5-game-goes-gold |website=Push Square |language=en-US |access-date=13 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Duckworth |first1=Joshua |date=13 May 2026 |title=007 First Light Has Officially Gone Gold |url=https://gamerant.com/007-first-light-gone-gold/ |website=Game Rant |language=en-US |access-date=13 May 2026}}</ref>

IO Interactive added a proprietary [[Volume rendering|volumetric]] smoke system to its Glacier engine for ''007 First Light'', which it claims "has not been done anywhere before". The game incorporates [[Ray tracing (graphics)|ray tracing]] and "fully dynamic" [[global illumination]] in its lighting model.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Garrett |first1=Ural |date=16 June 2025 |title=Hitman developer IO Interactive teams up with Nvidia to make its James Bond game look incredible |url=https://www.techradar.com/gaming/007-first-light-io-interactive-hitman-interview-sgf-2025 |website=TechRadar |language=en-US |access-date=16 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Judd |first1=William |date=28 May 2026 |title="They Understood the Assignment" – The 007 First Light Technology Review |url=https://www.digitalfoundry.net/features/they-understood-the-assignment-n-the-007-first-light-technology-review |website=Digital Foundry |language=en-US |access-date=28 May 2026}}</ref>

=== Gameplay development ===
IO Interactive took inspiration from the freeflow combat system in the ''[[Batman: Arkham]]'' series and the large action setpieces and destructible environments seen in the ''[[Uncharted]]'' series. In IO Interactive's ''[[Hitman: World of Assassination]]'' trilogy (2016–2021), combat was a last resort rather than the only viable option. The studio sought to design a combat system with ''007 First Light'' that flows seamlessly into cinematic setpieces.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bonthuys |first1=Darryn |date=23 February 2026 |title=007: First Light Aims To Channel Batman: Arkham Freeflow Combat With Uncharted Spectacle |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/007-first-light-aims-to-channel-batman-arkham-freeflow-combat-with-uncharted-spectacle/1100-6538356/ |website=GameSpot |language=en-US |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref> IO Interactive still aimed to maintain the ''Hitman'' series' freedom of choice in gameplay but wanted to avoid creating a "reskin" of ''Hitman''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ruiz |first1=Fran |date=25 February 2026 |title=007: First Light gameplay director talks Uncharted and Batman: Arkham influences that add to IO's Hitman pedigree |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/007-first-light-gameplay-director-talks-batman-arkham-and-uncharted-influences |website=Eurogamer |language=en-GB |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref> ''007 First Light'' emphasises greater forward momentum for the player's gameplay style whether that be in stealth or open combat compared to the slower, more deliberative, puzzle-like approach of ''Hitman'' where assassinations required setup.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gerblick |first1=Jordan |date=14 February 2026 |title=007: First Light will be less stealthy than Hitman because IO is pushing "forward momentum gameplay all the time" |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/games/hitman/007-first-light-will-be-less-stealthy-than-hitman-because-io-is-pushing-forward-momentum-gameplay-all-the-time/ |website=GamesRadar+ |language=en-GB |access-date=}}</ref> Unlike ''Hitman'', "you're playing as a spy, not an assassin" according to IO Interactive which puts greater emphasis on infiltration, investigation and eavesdropping on clues.<ref>{{cite web |last1=LeBlanc |first1=Wesley |date=2 September 2025 |title=Watching A Behind-Closed-Doors Demo Of 007 First Light Quelled My Biggest Worry |url=https://gameinformer.com/2025/09/02/watching-a-behind-closed-doors-demo-of-007-first-light-quelled-my-biggest-worry |website=Game Informer |language=en-US |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref>

''007 First Light'' is the first IO Interactive title to include drivable vehicles.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shea |first1=Brian |date=29 January 2026 |title=How 007 First Light Learns From And Moves Beyond Hitman |url=https://gameinformer.com/2026/01/29/how-007-first-light-learns-from-and-moves-beyond-hitman |website=Game Informer |language=en-US |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref> Art director Rasmus Poulsen described the inclusion of controllable vehicles as a "huge challenge" that the studio had to take on.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Joelle |date=4 September 2025 |title=007 First Light is Not a Reskin of Hitman – IO Interactive |url=https://gamingbolt.com/007-first-light-wont-be-a-reskin-of-hitman-io-interactive |website=GamingBolt |language=en-US |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref> The studio had to "bring onto the team specific driving expertise" in order to better incorporate such mechanics.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bailey |first1=Dustin |date=3 September 2025 |title=007 First Light is "not a reskin" of Hitman, IO Interactive says again, and the team brought in "amazing fresh talent" including devs with "specific driving expertise" to help build car missions |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/games/action/007-first-light-is-not-a-reskin-of-hitman-io-interactive-says-again-and-the-team-brought-in-amazing-fresh-talent-including-devs-with-specific-driving-expertise-to-help-build-car-missions/ |website=GamesRadar+ |language=en-GB |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref>

=== Character development ===
[[File:Patrick Gibson by Gage Skidmore.jpg|175px|thumb|right|[[Patrick Gibson (actor)|Patrick Gibson]] portrays a young James Bond in ''007 First Light''.]]
As no actor had been cast to succeed [[Daniel Craig]] as Bond for future films at the time of the game's development, IO Interactive felt a sense of freedom in crafting their own version of Bond that did not have to be based on an existing Bond actor or to be a video game adaptation of the films. IO Interactive CEO Hakan Abrak said, "I don't think we would have necessarily had the same energy and the same vision and the same results if we were to do a gamification of a movie."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shea |first1=Brian |date=28 January 2026 |title=How IO Interactive Crafted Its Young Version Of James Bond |url=https://gameinformer.com/2026/01/28/how-io-interactive-crafted-its-young-version-of-james-bond |website=Game Informer |language=en-US |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref> ''007 Legends'' included an adaptation of one film from every Bond actor and heavily incorporated elements from the films to coincide with the release of ''[[Skyfall]]'' (2012), while using Craig's likeness for Bond.

In creating its own version of Bond, IO Interactive sought to create something new and unique while still honouring the character's legacy. ''007 First Light'' follows a 26-year-old Bond as a recruit in the MI6 training program. Irish actor [[Patrick Gibson (actor)|Patrick Gibson]] was cast as Bond. Gibson said he was "pretty stunned" after learning he had been cast.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Karunakar |first1=Varun |date=16 May 2026 |title=007 First Light’s James Bond Actor Was “Pretty Stunned” to Learn Of His Casting |url=https://gamingbolt.com/007-first-lights-james-bond-actor-was-pretty-stunned-to-learn-of-his-casting |website=GamingBolt |language=en-US |access-date=16 May 2026}}</ref> Narrative and cinematic director Martin Emborg said that Gibson had a level of "built-in impatience" that was "perfect" for a young Bond.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Makuch |first1=Eddie |date=29 January 2026 |title=Patrick Gibson's "Impatience" Made Him Perfect For Young James Bond In 007 First Light, Dev Says |url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/patrick-gibsons-impatience-made-him-perfect-for-young-james-bond-in-007-first-light-dev-says/1100-6537763/ |website=GameSpot |language=en-US |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref> Emborg wanted the young Bond to exhibit "an unearned confidence" that he hoped players would read as a glaring naivety from "a reckless young man".<ref name="Purchese 2026">{{cite web |last1=Purchese |first1=Robert |date=14 May 2026 |title="If we made a Bond where no one had any opinions on them, it would be the dullest Bond ever made" - 007: First Light studio reacts to suggestion its Bond is too smug |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/007-first-light-james-bond-smug |website=Eurogamer |language=en-GB |access-date=14 May 2026}}</ref> Senior combat designer Tom Marcham wanted the game's combat to exhibit the character's "inner rage" from his childhood experiences as an orphan.<ref name="Purchese 2026"/>

When developing the characters surrounding Bond, IO Interactive paid mind to how they influence Bond's personality and mannerisms as he grows into a skilled MI6 agent.<ref name="Zimmer">{{cite web |last1=Zimmer |first1=Evan |date=4 March 2026 |title=007 First Light Reveals New Details About Its Characters |url=https://gamerant.com/007-first-light-characters/ |website=Game Rant |language=en-US |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref> Emborg said that they imbued surrounding characters like M and Moneypenny with "some of those qualities that you know from Bond, and so that they can inform the character". Moneypenny plays a more active role in ''007 First Light'' as a field analyst who assists Bond in the field rather than simply being M's secretary as in the original stories.<ref name="Zimmer"/> The character played a similar role in the field during ''Skyfall''{{'}}s prologue sequence. Moneypenny is voiced by Kiera Lester. With the exception of [[Judi Dench]], [[M (James Bond)|M]] is typically portrayed by an older male actor, inspired by Fleming's own superior officer at the [[Naval Intelligence Division (United Kingdom)|Naval Intelligence Division]]. [[Priyanga Burford]]'s version of M in ''007 First Light'' is younger than previous iterations of the character and actively supports and encourages Bond's growth as an agent rather than clashing with him as in previous depictions. John Greenway, portrayed by [[Lennie James]], is an original character created for the game and a senior MI6 field agent, conceived as a 'mentor figure'.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-07-21 |title=007 First Light's secret best character was a perfect way for IO Interactive to celebrate British writing and "restrained emotion" |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/007-first-light-britishness-john-greenway |access-date=2026-07-23 |work=Eurogamer.net |language=en}}</ref> Q is portrayed as older than the previous iteration of the character by [[Ben Whishaw]] in the Craig films, though not as old as [[Desmond Llewelyn]] or [[John Cleese]]. Actor [[Alastair Mackenzie]] played Q as more befitting the "cool uncle figure" he viewed the character as when growing up.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sinha |first1=Ravi |date=5 March 2026 |title=007 First Light Dev Diary Outlines the Cast, Including Alastair Mackenzie as Q |url=https://gamingbolt.com/007-first-light-dev-diary-outlines-the-cast-including-alastair-mackenzie-as-q |website=GamingBolt |language=en-US |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref>

=== Music ===
{{Further|First Light (song)}}
[[File:LanaDRPrimavera310524 (32 of 147) (53765476960) (cropped).jpg|upright|right|thumb|[[Lana Del Rey]] sings the game's theme song, "[[First Light (song)|First Light]]".]]
The musical score for ''007 First Light'' was composed by [[The Flight (band)|the Flight]]. IO Interactive felt that they were the right choice to score a younger Bond as they could blend cinematic [[orchestral music]] with more modern [[Electronic music|electronic]] textures that had not been heard in the ''Bond'' franchise before. While classic [[John Barry (composer)|John Barry]] themes feature, audio director Dominic Vega said that the young Bond has to "earn his themes" as he grows throughout the game's story.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Donaldson |first1=Alex |date=8 September 2025 |title=Developer IO Interactive on why Bond needs to "earn" his iconic theme music in 007: First Light |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/developer-io-interactive-on-why-bond-needs-to-earn-hiss-iconic-theme-music-in-007-first-light |website=Eurogamer |language=en-GB |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref>

In October 2025, reports emerged that a song called "[[First Light (song)|First Light]]" by American singer-songwriter [[Lana Del Rey]] was registered with the [[American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers]] (ASCAP).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Koepp |first1=Brent |date=20 October 2025 |title=007 First Light Theme Song Artist Reportedly Leaked |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/007-first-light-theme-song-artist-reportedly-leaked/ |website=Vice |language=en-US |access-date=16 April 2026}}</ref> On 16 April 2026, "First Light" was revealed as the game's theme song; it was co-written and produced by ''James Bond'' film composer [[David Arnold]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pinder |first1=Jaeden |date=16 April 2026 |title=Lana Del Rey Drops Orchestral Title Song for '007 First Light' Video Game |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/lana-del-rey-007-first-light-video-game-title-song-1235548242/ |website=Rolling Stone |language=en-US |access-date=16 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Romano |first1=Nick |date=16 April 2026 |title=From 'Video Games' to video games, Lana Del Rey records new James Bond theme song for 007: First Light |url=https://ew.com/lana-del-rey-james-bond-theme-song-007-first-light-11950902 |website=Entertainment Weekly |language=en-US |access-date=16 April 2026}}</ref> Del Rey had previously submitted the song "24" for Craig's film ''[[Spectre (2015 film)|Spectre]]'' (2015), which was rejected: Del Rey instead included the song on her fourth studio album, ''[[Honeymoon (Lana Del Rey album)|Honeymoon]]'' (2015).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pandey |first1=Manish |date=16 April 2026 |title=Lana Del Rey to sing theme for new James Bond game |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c4gx984j49ro |website=BBC News |language=en-GB |access-date=16 April 2026}}</ref> ''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]'' wrote that Del Rey's "First Light" is "fully committed to the storied legacy of ''Bond'' themes, even to a fault" with its jangling guitar and orchestral swells.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Colantonio |first1=Giovanni |date=16 April 2026 |title=Track review: Lana Del Rey's "First Light" |url=https://www.polygon.com/lana-del-rey-007-first-light-track-review/ |website=Polygon |language=en-US |access-date=18 April 2026}}</ref> The game's soundtrack album by  the Flight, was released on 31 July 2026 by [[Milan Records]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleedingcool.com/pop-culture/milan-records-releases-the-007-first-light-soundtrack/|title=Milan Records Releases The 007 First Light Soundtrack|website=Bleeding Cool|first=Gavin|last=Sheehan|date=31 July 2026|access-date=1 August 2026}}</ref>

== Release ==
[[IO Interactive]] held a livestream on 19 November 2020 to announce their next game following the then-upcoming ''[[Hitman 3]]'' (2021),<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chalk |first=Andy |date=18 November 2020 |title=Hitman studio IO Interactive will reveal a new project tomorrow morning |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-studio-io-interactive-will-reveal-a-new-project-tomorrow-morning/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201118192740/https://www.pcgamer.com/hitman-studio-io-interactive-will-reveal-a-new-project-tomorrow-morning/ |archive-date=18 November 2020 |website=PC Gamer |language=en-US |access-date=21 April 2025}}</ref> which concluded with the reveal of ''Project 007'', a new ''James Bond'' video game with an original story developed and published by IOI, in collaboration with Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, Eon Productions, and licensee Delphi Interactive.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ruppert |first=Liana |date=19 November 2020 |title=IO Interactive's New Game Is A 007 James Bond Origins Story |url=https://www.gameinformer.com/2020/11/19/io-interactives-new-game-is-a-007-james-bond-origins-story |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201119145222/https://gameinformer.com/2020/11/19/io-interactives-new-game-is-a-007-james-bond-origins-story |archive-date=19 November 2020 |website=[[Game Informer]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The announcement coincided with the official start of development at IOI's Denmark and Sweden studios.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 November 2020 |title=Announcing Project 007 |url=https://ioi.dk/careers/news/2020/announcing-project-007 |website=[[IO Interactive]] |access-date=21 April 2025}}</ref> The game is being developed on the [[Glacier Engine]] for "modern systems and platforms".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barker |first=Sammy |date=19 November 2020 |title=Project 007 Targeting Modern Systems, Will Run on Glacier Engine |url=https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2020/11/project_007_targeting_modern_systems_will_run_on_glacier_engine |url-status=live |website=[[Push Square]] |language=en-GB |access-date=21 April 2025}}</ref> In February 2025, [[Amazon MGM Studios]] took over supervisory duties on the title after acquiring full creative and production rights to the ''James Bond'' IP from Eon and former film franchise producers [[Michael G. Wilson]] and [[Barbara Broccoli]], making it the first ''Bond'' game to be released since Eon's departure from the series.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Svetkey |first=Benjamin |date=7 March 2025 |title=License to Shill: Inside Amazon's 007 Takeover |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/amazon-007-takeover-impact-future-james-bond-1236155844/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250307144437/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/amazon-007-takeover-impact-future-james-bond-1236155844/ |archive-date=7 March 2025 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Zalben |first=Alex |date=21 February 2025 |title=The Bond Franchise Sale to Amazon MGM Is Probably Bad News... But Here Are Some Ways It Could Work |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/the-bond-franchise-sale-to-amazon-mgm-is-probably-bad-news-but-here-are-some-ways-it-could-work |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250221183203/https://www.ign.com/articles/the-bond-franchise-sale-to-amazon-mgm-is-probably-bad-news-but-here-are-some-ways-it-could-work |archive-date=21 February 2025 |website=IGN |language=en-US |access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref> The game was confirmed to be launching on [[Nintendo Switch 2]] during the April 2025 instalment of [[Nintendo Direct]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kennedy |first=Victoria |date=2 April 2025 |title=IOI's James Bond game confirmed for Switch 2 |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/iois-james-bond-game-confirmed-for-switch-2 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250402180710/https://www.eurogamer.net/iois-james-bond-game-confirmed-for-switch-2 |archive-date=2 April 2025 |website=Eurogamer |language=en-GB |access-date=21 April 2025}}</ref>

The game was originally announced to be released for [[Nintendo Switch 2]], [[PlayStation 5]], [[Windows]], and [[Xbox Series X/S]] on 27 March 2026.<ref name="Roskell" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Webster |first=Andrew |date=4 June 2025 |title=James Bond game 007 First Light gets first trailer |url=https://www.theverge.com/news/679909/007-first-light-trailer-james-bond |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250604215332/https://www.theverge.com/news/679909/007-first-light-trailer-james-bond |archive-date=4 June 2025 |website=The Verge |language=en-US |access-date=5 June 2025}}</ref> In December 2025, the release date was delayed to 27 May 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Jay |date=23 December 2025 |title=007 First Light's release date gets shaken up |url=https://www.theverge.com/news/849810/james-bond-007-first-light-release-date-delay |website=The Verge |language=en-US |access-date=24 December 2025}}</ref> In April 2026, the Nintendo Switch 2 version was delayed to the third quarter of 2026.<ref>{{cite web|last=Romano|first=Sal|date=8 April 2026|title=007 First Light for Switch 2 delayed to "later this summer" |url=https://www.gematsu.com/2026/04/007-first-light-for-switch-2-delayed-to-later-this-summer|website=Gematsu|access-date=8 April 2026}}</ref> IO Interactive CEO Hakan Abrak stated that the developers pushed it to later in the summer season to allow more work on optimization, but that they were working to get it ready due to the legacy of ''Bond'' games on Nintendo platforms.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reynolds |first=Ollie |date=5 May 2026 |title="I Will Do Everything I Can" - IO Interactive Boss Promises 007 First Light Won't Pull A Borderlands 4 |url=https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2026/05/i-will-do-everything-i-can-io-interactive-boss-promises-007-first-light-wont-pull-a-borderlands-4 |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=Nintendo Life |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Promotion ===
IO Interactive partnered with [[Coca-Cola]] for promotion of ''007 First Light'' with themed cans of Zero Sugar Zero Caffeine offering competition prizes, including in-game outfits for Bond and a one-of-a-kind ''007 First Light''-themed Xbox Series X.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zero Caffeine, Anytime Refreshment, Epic Prizes |url=https://www.coca-cola.com/gb/en/offerings/zero-caffeine-anytime-refreshment |website=Coca-Cola |language=en-GB |access-date=14 May 2026}}</ref> From 14 May to 10 June 2026, a free copy of ''007 First Light'' is bundled with the purchase of an Nvidia [[GeForce RTX 50 series]] graphics card.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Andreadis |first1=Kosta |title=New GeForce Bundle offers 007 First Light with new GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs and systems |url=https://www.tweaktown.com/news/111599/new-geforce-bundle-offers-007-first-light-with-new-geforce-rtx-50-series-gpus-and-systems/index.html |website=TweakTown |language=en-US |access-date=14 May 2026}}</ref>

==Reception==
=== Critical reception ===

''007 First Light'' received "generally favorable" reviews, according to [[review aggregator]] website [[Metacritic]].<ref name="MCPC"/><ref name="MCPS5"/><ref name="MCXSXS"/>

Writing for ''[[Eurogamer]]'', Rick Lane felt that ''007 First Light'' "isn't the Bond game that I wanted from IO Interactive [...] [b]ut I had a great time with it regardless". He especially praised the game's writing, noting that "almost every line lands with wit, soul, or both", and describing it as the best-written AAA game since ''[[Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy]]''. Lane commended Bond's characterization, noting how the "younger and more unrefined" Bond present in the game was also "perhaps the most empathetic Bond yet", but felt that "the real surprise in ''First Light'' is how strong the secondary cast is", praising the variety of the game's original characters. Regarding the gameplay, Lane noted that ''007 First Light'' is largely a linear [[action-adventure game]], but "frequently pretends that it isn't". He felt that the game occasionally pretended to open up and provide the player with a number of possible solutions, but ultimately funnelled them towards a specific intended path. However, he praised the game's [[close-quarters combat]], as well as its "bluffing" mechanic, which he saw as a novel addition. Lane noted that despite what he felt were immensely enjoyable levels, many of them existed not as distinct locations, but as "spaces that Bond is just passing through on the way to his next objective", hurting their memorability.<ref name="EuroG"/>

Mark Delaney of ''[[GameSpot]]'' very directly compared ''007 First Light'' to the ''[[Hitman (franchise)|Hitman]]'' franchise, also developed by IO Interactive. He specifically called out the frequency of needing to distract or otherwise sneak past guards, hanging from ledges or pipes, eavesdropping on conversations, and lying to enemies, all of which he noted were staples of ''Hitman''. Delaney complimented the game's hand-to-hand combat systems, especially praising the interactivity of the environment in combat. He also praised the gunplay, noting how guns "never have much ammo with them", which requires the player to "frequently change what [they're] armed with by taking them off defeated enemies". Delaney additionally praised how well he felt the franchise's tropes fit into the structure of a video game, noting the versatility of gadgets that helped "ensure the spirit of the Bond character is alive". However, he criticized the pacing, feeling that ''007 First Light''{{'}}s 20-hour runtime resulted in some sections that were significantly slower than others.<ref name="GSpot"/>

Amelia Schwanke of ''[[TechRadar]]'' commended ''007 First Light''{{'}}s cinematic sequences, stating that "IO Interactive has managed to make a [...] game that truly feels like you’re playing a James Bond in a movie". She complimented the cinematic training montage towards the beginning of the game, which she said felt "straight out of a [[Rocky (franchise)|''Rocky'']] film, quickly switching you from one exercise to the next". Schwanke noted that this cinematic attention to detail was spread throughout the entire game, and was especially visible in the original depiction of James Bond with "no [[Daniel Craig]] or [[Pierce Brosnan]] shadow hanging over him". She also noted Bond's cocky attitude, which came off as "more eye-roll inducing than funny", but felt it worked in the game's favor due to Bond being far younger and less refined than in other depictions. She praised the variety and open-ended nature of the stealth sequences, although she noted that they were significantly "stripped back" compared to the [[Sandbox game|sandbox]] gameplay of ''Hitman''. Schwanke also praised the gadget system, which she felt was reminiscent of the ''[[Batman: Arkham]]'' games, as well as the cinematic variety of the game's setpieces, which she compared to Naughty Dog's ''[[Uncharted]]'' series. However, she noted the frequency of physics-related glitches, as well as the driving sections, which she felt were "tacked on" due to their legacy in the ''Bond'' franchise and "not nearly as dynamic as [they] could've been".<ref name="TR"/>

=== Sales ===
''007 First Light'' sold 1.5 million units within the first day of release.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Croft|first=Liam|date=28 May 2026 |title=007 First Light Debuts to 1.5 Million Sales in Just 24 Hours |url=https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2026/05/007-first-light-debuts-to-1-5-million-sales-in-just-24-hours |access-date=28 May 2026 |website=[[Push Square]]|language=en-GB}}</ref> The game sold 2.7 million units within the first week of release.<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 June 2026 |title=IO Interactive's James Bond game 007 First Light sells 2.7 million copies in its first week, as dev reiterates free Year One content |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/io-interactives-james-bond-game-007-first-light-sells-27-million-copies-in-its-first-week-as-dev-reiterates-free-year-one-content |access-date=6 June 2026 |work=Eurogamer.net |language=en}}</ref> It had sold 4 million units by 20 August 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sinha |first=Ravi |title=007 First Light Has Sold 4 Million Units |url=https://gamingbolt.com/007-first-light-has-sold-4-million-units |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=GamingBolt |language=en-US}}</ref>

In Japan, the game debuted at #2 on the top 20 games sold in the country from 25–31 May.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2026-06-08/japan-video-game-rankings-may-25-31/.238271|title=Japan's Video Game Rankings, May 25-31 |date=9 June 2026|last1=Pineda|first1=Rafael Antonio|publisher=Anime News Network}}</ref> The game debuted at #1 in the United Kingdom.<ref>{{Cite news |last=D'Angelo |first=William |date=1 June 2026 |title=007 First Light Debuts in 1st on the UK Retail Charts |url=https://www.vgchartz.com/article/467985/007-first-light-debuts-in-1st-on-the-uk-retail-charts/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260611133214/https://www.vgchartz.com/article/467985/007-first-light-debuts-in-1st-on-the-uk-retail-charts/ |archive-date=11 June 2026 |access-date=22 June 2026 |work=VGChartz |language=en-US}}</ref>{{clear}}

== Future ==
IO Interactive CEO Hakan Abrak expressed in an interview with ''[[IGN]]'' that he wished for ''007 First Light'' to lead into a potential trilogy of ''James Bond'' video games for the publisher, citing the decision to create a new, younger version of the character for gaming audiences to "call their own and grow with".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tailby |first=Stephen |date=17 October 2024 |title=IO Interactive's Project 007 to Feature a 'Young Bond for Gamers' with a View to a Trilogy |url=https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2024/10/io-interactives-project-007-to-feature-a-young-bond-for-gamers-with-a-view-to-a-trilogy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241021133346/https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2024/10/io-interactives-project-007-to-feature-a-young-bond-for-gamers-with-a-view-to-a-trilogy |archive-date=21 October 2024 |website=Push Square |language=en-GB |access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref> Abrak previously stated his desire to progress the ''James Bond'' narrative through "multiple" games in a similar fashion to the ''Hitman: World of Assassination'' trilogy, stating that such an ambition motivated them to pursue a licencing deal after previously rejecting offers for other video games using external properties.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stanton |first=Rich |date=9 November 2023 |title=IO got the 007 license because it wants to make 'multiple Bond games' in the same way it handled Hitman |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/io-got-the-007-license-because-it-wants-to-make-multiple-bond-games-in-the-same-way-it-handled-hitman/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231110022301/https://www.pcgamer.com/io-got-the-007-license-because-it-wants-to-make-multiple-bond-games-in-the-same-way-it-handled-hitman/ |archive-date=10 November 2023 |website=PC Gamer |language=en-US |access-date=22 April 2025}}</ref> Following the game's release, [[Amazon Game Studios]] general manager Jeff Gattis confirmed that following [[Amazon MGM Studios]]' acquisition of the franchise license from [[Eon Productions]] in 2025, future ''James Bond'' games, including sequels to ''First Light'', would be published in-house as opposed to IO Interactive's self-publishing arrangement on this title.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chalk |first=Andy |date=3 June 2026 |title=007 First Light sequels will be 'done by MGM and, theoretically, by Amazon Game Studios,' Amazon exec says |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/action/007-first-light-sequels-will-be-done-by-mgm-and-theoretically-by-amazon-game-studios-amazon-exec-says/ |access-date=4 June 2026 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}}</ref>However, Gattis later appeared to walk back the statement, suggesting that audiences "probably want IOI developing [a sequel]" given the success of the game and further clarifying that no decisions had been made on Amazon's potential involvement.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Packwood |first=Lewis |date=2026-07-23 |title=Amazon clarifies stance on 007: First Light sequel – "Given the success of this one, I think you probably want IOI developing it" |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/amazon-clarifies-stance-on-007-first-light-sequel-given-the-success-of-this-one-i-think-you-probably-want-ioi-developing-it |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=GamesIndustry.biz |language=en}}</ref>
